title: P46: uniform checkpoint average over the final 20% of pretraining
description: P46: hand fixed downstream expert iteration the equal-weight parameter average at 80%, 85%, 90%, 95% and the end of the pretraining wall-clock budget instead of the final raw checkpoint. This tests whether smoothing the late split-QKV Muon trajectory produces a more transferable policy while preserving every optimizer update rule and the model architecture.
hypothesis: Incumbent 043 uses orthogonal initialization and split-QKV Nesterov Muon, scoring 282/275/269 (exact mean 275.333333). P45 run 025 failed with per-step EMA decay 0.99 under the earlier AdamW baseline (mean 81 versus 148); this is a distinct fixed finite-window uniform average on the Muon incumbent, not a repeat of that configuration. Averaging late weights could retain proof features shared across nearby iterates while reducing endpoint-specific noise, improving RL discovery and its compounding gains. The negative EMA evidence lowers the prior: averaging may instead blur useful specialization or introduce lag, and lower pretraining loss is not a success criterion. P46 has no earlier registration. The fixed downstream three-seed mean alone determines keep/discard.
expected_delta: Conditional on improvement, +3 to +15 dev-transfer >=7 solves versus exact baseline mean 275.333333; plausible downside -20 to -60. Expect less than 1% pretraining overhead from five averaging operations and the initial copy, with no RL/inference latency increase; all work is charged to the unchanged budget.

optimizer.name: split-QKV Muon hidden matrices throughout; continuous AdamW auxiliary

muon.precision: bf16 Newton-Schulz; fp32 momentum and parameters
muon.shape_scale: sqrt(max(1, rows/columns)) per orthogonalized matrix: Q/K/V each 1, attention output 1, fc1 2, fc2 1
muon.schedule: same warmup/cosine fraction as AdamW; muon_lr = 0.01 * adam_lr / 0.001
muon.parameters: All 16 hidden projection parameters remain in Muon. Four qkv.weight matrices of shape (768,256) use independent Q/K/V updates, represented as a batch of three (256,256) matrices; proj/fc1/fc2 remain unchanged.
muon.license: MIT; full copyright and permission notice retained in pretrain.py
muon.qkv_split: After elementwise Nesterov momentum, reshape each QKV update to (3,256,256); independently Frobenius-normalize and run five batched Newton-Schulz steps; reshape back before applying. No extra learning-rate multiplier. Momentum and weight decay stay elementwise and unchanged.

optimizer.adamw_parameters: emb.weight, head.weight, all projection biases and LayerNorm parameters throughout; hidden matrices never enter pretraining AdamW
optimizer.decay_convention: Muon lr*0.01 equals auxiliary AdamW lr*0.1, preserving incumbent per-update shrinkage at every schedule fraction, including the former finish window; integrated decay can differ with throughput.
optimizer.clipping: joint global gradient norm 1.0 before both optimizers
optimizer.handoff: Uniform five-checkpoint averaged standard GPT weights only; pretraining optimizer states and averaging copy are discarded and frozen RL creates its own unchanged AdamW

config.init: Fork default construction, then orthogonal_ on every 2D block parameter after moving to device. Gain = 0.02 * sqrt(max(rows, columns)); exact element second moment 0.0004. All 16 hidden matrices: qkv (768,256), proj (256,256), fc1 (1024,256), fc2 (256,1024) in each of four blocks. QKV initialized jointly. Embedding, readout, biases and LayerNorm retain their original draws/values. No reinitialization during RL.

checkpoint_average.method: equal-weight arithmetic mean of all parameters using torch.optim.swa_utils.AveragedModel; no auxiliary trainable heads
checkpoint_average.timing: First loop boundary at or after each of 0.80, 0.85, 0.90 and 0.95 of budget, before the next update; fifth snapshot is the final raw weights at loop exit. Expected snapshot times 240/255/270/285/300 seconds. No metric-based selection.
checkpoint_average.handoff: Load averaged.module.state_dict into the original plain fork GPT, then eval; the averaging copy and all pretraining optimizer state are discarded. RL trains ordinary GPT parameters with its frozen procedure.
checkpoint_average.diagnostics: curve and last_loss describe raw training weights; averaging_steps records actual snapshot update indices. Held-out greedy and downstream RL use averaged weights.
checkpoint_average.storage: One additional 3210240-parameter model copy during pretraining; 6420480 total parameters across original and averaging copy, below 10000000; returned GPT has 3210240 parameters.
